title: Remove quantitative Hunch metrics from boilerplate docs
context: Hunch statistics (decision/bug/constraint counts) were hardcoded in instruction files and regenerated by an external MCP server. These counts became stale when Hunch's actual database changed, causing drift between the in-tree CLI generator and globally-installed MCP versions.
decision: Remove specific Hunch metrics (254 decisions, 2 bugs, 28 constraints, etc.) from all instruction/rule files. Keep the conceptual description of Hunch but omit quantitative claims that require active maintenance to stay current.
consequences: Docs no longer diverge when Hunch grows/shrinks — no stale metrics to regenerate
Users must consult actual MCP tools (`hunch_*` commands) to see current Hunch scope
Simpler regeneration process — no numerical sync burden between generators
Avoids false precision in instruction files that users rarely update
alternatives_rejected: Keep counts and regenerate them with every Hunch change (high maintenance, still prone to drift)
Add 'last checked' timestamps to acknowledge staleness (still inaccurate, doesn't solve the problem)
Maintain counts in one canonical file and sync to others (single point of failure)
